_comment: Source of truth for crash-dump settings. golden-image-pre-reboot.ps1 writes the same values into the golden image and golden-image-post-reboot.ps1 verifies them; at run time validate-crash-settings.ps1 only compares the live registry with recommended.values (value and type) and recommended.absentValues and reports mismatches without changing anything. 'crashDumpType' values follow the CrashDumpEnabled registry semantics.
_source: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl. See Microsoft docs: 'Overview of memory dump file options for Windows'.

complete.description: Complete memory dump: entire physical memory. Requires a page file >= RAM size (+1MB); this project does not use a dedicated dump file.

kernel.description: Kernel memory dump: kernel-mode read/write pages only. Good default for driver crashes.

automatic.description: Automatic memory dump (Win8+): like kernel dump but lets the OS manage page-file sizing.

filtered.description: Variable size. Filters out VM host/guest memory overhead, making offline extraction faster than full complete dumps on high-RAM servers.

recommended.notes: CrashDumpEnabled=7 (Automatic). AutoReboot=0 stops Windows from rebooting itself after the simulated crash, so the frozen VM keeps its memory for capture (src/scripts/host/watch-crash.sh still starts the VM again afterwards unless it runs with --no-restart). Dumps go through the page file only: golden-image-pre-reboot.ps1 configures a fixed C:\pagefile.sys of RAM + 257 MB and no DedicatedDumpFile. Small (mini) dumps are not part of this flow. KubeVirt vm-memory.elf.tar.gz captures full physical memory and the disk is extracted offline.

pageFile.notes: Adequate when PagingFiles holds an entry on C: ("<path> <initialMB> <maxMB>") whose initial and maximum sizes are both at least physical RAM + 257 MB, the size golden-image-pre-reboot.ps1 configures. System-managed or missing page files are not adequate; DedicatedDumpFile is not used.
